title: India's Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
gist: Shekhar Aiyar argues India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump's return to the White House specifically to ensure no single bilateral rupture can cause catastrophic harm, and urges India to keep expanding trade ties while avoiding any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action toward third countries; this is a paywalled teaser excerpt.

insights.claim: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump's return to the White House specifically as a hedging strategy, so that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic economic harm.
insights.speaker: Shekhar Aiyar
insights.so_what: Frames India's recent trade-deal wave as deliberate geopolitical risk diversification rather than pure economic opportunism -- relevant for assessing India's resilience to a future US-India trade dispute.
insights.quote: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump's return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm.

insights.claim: India signed a free trade agreement with the United Kingdom last year, followed in January by a wide-ranging agreement with the European Union described as the 'mother of all deals,' while high-level trade talks with the United States continue, building on a joint statement of intent issued in February.
insights.speaker: Shekhar Aiyar
insights.so_what: A concrete timeline of India's major trade-deal activity (UK FTA, EU deal in January, ongoing US talks since February) gives investors a trackable sequence for assessing India's market-access expansion and remaining negotiation risk with the US.
insights.locator: Last year's free trade agreement (FTA) with the United Kingdom

insights.claim: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi used his participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Council meeting in Kyrgyzstan to push for deeper trade links between member states, in addition to the meeting's regional security agenda.
insights.speaker: Shekhar Aiyar
insights.so_what: Shows India actively using multilateral security forums (SCO) to also advance trade diversification, indicating trade diplomacy is now embedded across multiple diplomatic channels, not confined to bilateral talks.
insights.locator: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's participation

insights.claim: The author recommends India continue expanding its trade ties while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.
insights.speaker: Shekhar Aiyar
insights.so_what: A specific watch-point for evaluating any future India-US trade deal: whether its terms impose restrictions on India's dealings with other countries (e.g., Russia, China) as a hidden cost of market access.
insights.quote: It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.
